# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can physically operate only the button or cut one of the three wires, but I have no access to the manual or the bomb’s visible colours and markings. I need Mute to relay the manual’s rule and Deaf to identify the visible wire/button information before touching anything.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please report the manual's exact defusal procedure, including whether to push the button or cut a wire and any required conditions.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Display 0. Light yellow. Large button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires top to bottom: red, blue, green.

The bomb’s physical layout is now known: the display reads 0, the light is yellow, the button is marked “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” and the wires are red, blue, then green from top to bottom. I still need the manual’s rule before acting, so I am asking Mute to provide it and relaying the observed details.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, yellow light, button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires top to bottom red, blue, green. What exact manual rule applies?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No change: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires top to bottom red blue green.

Mute has not supplied the manual rule yet, so I cannot safely choose an operation. The visible facts remain unchanged; I will request the manual’s exact instruction again rather than risk pushing or cutting.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I still have not received the manual. Please send its exact rule now, including the required action and any display, light, colour, or wire conditions.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's Morse clearly says DO NOT PUSH. The remaining message appears intended as CUT BLUE, but two Morse groups are malformed. Blue is wire 2, between red and green.

The only clear instruction is not to push. Cutting the blue wire is suggested, and Deaf identifies blue as wire 2, but the malformed Morse groups make that instruction insufficiently reliable for an irreversible cut. I will ask Mute to resend the complete instruction unambiguously through Deaf.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please resend the entire manual instruction clearly to Deaf, confirming whether the action is CUT BLUE and whether that means wire 2. Do not omit or abbreviate any Morse groups.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red blue green top to bottom. I cannot reliably decode Mute's latest gesture stream; Morse interpretation is incoherent. Do not act on my wire or button guess.

The bomb remains unchanged, and Deaf cannot reliably decode the latest transmission. Since Mute cannot speak, I will establish a simple unambiguous gesture code: 👎 means do not push, 👍 means push, and ☝/✌/🤟 identify wires 1/2/3. Mute should send the manual’s required action using that code, with any conditions represented in a clear ordered sequence.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use clear gestures, not Morse. For the action send 👍 for PUSH or 👎 for DO NOT PUSH, then ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3. Repeat the full required instruction, including any condition, in an ordered sequence so Deaf can report each symbol exactly.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red blue green. Mute sent two Morse-like messages, but neither decodes coherently enough to authorize an action. Do not press or cut anything yet.

No reliable instruction has arrived, so acting remains unsafe. I will reduce the communication to one symbol at a time: Mute should send exactly one gesture, with no Morse or sequence, first indicating whether the manual requires pushing. Deaf can then identify that single gesture precisely; wire identification can follow separately if needed.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Send exactly ONE gesture next turn, with no Morse and no sequence: 👍 means PUSH, 👎 means DO NOT PUSH. Deaf should report the single symbol exactly.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute just gestured thumbs-down, then V/peace sign. No wire or button instruction can be safely inferred from only these two gestures. Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red blue green.
Mute gestures: [?]

Mute’s latest two gestures match the code I explicitly established: thumbs-down means do not push, and the V/peace sign means wire 2. This also agrees with the earlier partial report “DO NOT PUSH” and “CUT BLUE,” while the blue wire is confirmed as position 2. I will therefore cut wire 2.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
